## v0.23.0 — correctness batch

Every change below went through per-PR adversarial review with RED/GREEN receipts, and every
score-sensitive change carries an architect verdict on the eval queue (#252) plus a boundary
row in `bench/BASELINE-LEDGER.md`.

### Data integrity / replay-proof (reconcile)
- **#177** — partial tool tails replay correctly after restart; replay proofs are now
  occurrence-bounded (a genuinely repeated identical invocation is persisted, never dropped)
  and replay identity includes the executing tool's name. Note: replay-snapshot digests
  change once — the first restart after upgrading a session with live registered digests
  re-persists instead of matching (visible duplication, never loss).
- **#203** — Hermes-generated replay scaffolding is normalized; out-of-band block durability
  proofs are bound to a unique row identity, and ID-less rows fail closed (persisted).
- **#259** — the fork/side-channel ingest guard is removed (architect veto with a proven
  replay repro); the silent-drop contract is fenced by a permanent regression test. Its
  successor design is tracked in #260.

### Retrieval
- **#173** — a slow full-text arm can no longer starve semantic recall: arm-local sub-budget
  with a hardened corpus preflight (independent scan budget, session-scope awareness,
  cap-attribution requires an actually-elapsed deadline).
- **#183** — summary DAG expansion works across sessions (`lcm_describe`/`lcm_expand`/
  `lcm_expand_query` accept explicit session ids) with correct per-session provenance.
- **#184** — sessions can be excluded from memory retrieval (hard filters before fusion).
- **#273** — a crashed full-text search now reports `coverage.fts: 'none'` with a reason,
  never an `'ok'` empty result indistinguishable from an empty corpus.
- **#172** — the Voyage reranker is configurable.

### Reliability / operations
- **#261** — fresh-database FTS bootstrap race fixed; integrity state now publishes only
  with proof valid at publish time (verified-pass clearing; CAS-fenced background-scan
  publish that errs toward recorded evidence).
- **#179** — doctor scan no longer flags incidental payload refs.
- **#168** — `lcm_status` exposes a durable total-compactions counter (best-effort accuracy
  contract documented in #288).
- **#198** — summary and expansion reasoning effort are separately configurable; invalid
  config values warn-and-ignore (owner-ratified posture), surfaced via `lcm_status`/doctor.

### Teams (candidate machinery — NOT enabled)
- **#286** — slice 1 of the LCM Teams v1 extraction: the `AccessContextV1` contract package
  (validation ladder, denial projection, 54 shared fixture vectors, authority-path
  inventory). Pure additive; nothing consumes it yet; standard single-user behavior is
  entirely unchanged. Enablement remains a separate, pilot-gated decision (#75, #83).

### Tests / docs
- **#254, #257** — regression coverage salvaged from closed PRs (#159/#160/#191).
- **#262** — gpt-5.4 retirement recorded in codex routing docs.
- Benchmark program work continued under `bench/` (compaction-quality pilot instruments,
  drivers, baseline ledger) — no runtime effect.

### NOT included (known gaps, tracked)
- **#90** (P1: recovered session follows stale summary) — under repro-first investigation;
  ships in this release only if the fix lands before the final tag, otherwise first
  follow-up.
- **#244** (FTS trigger repair transactionality) — accepted follow-up; CI-only repro.
- **#288** (durable-counter edge-regime accuracy), **#265** (FTS-cap engagement in degraded
  semantic states), **#260** (positive fork provenance) — accepted follow-ups with revisit
  triggers.
- Teams slices 2–5 (policy/catalog, scope columns, read/write hooks) — target v0.24.0,
  dormant; architect-gated per slice.
- Architect-held PRs (#161 #163 #165 #191 #201 #205) and the owner queue (#166 #188 #189
  #197 #206 #223) — unchanged.
